title: viz!: add isomesh keyword for solid 3D isosurfaces
abstract:
## Summary `viz!` gets an `isomesh=level` keyword for 3D plots: the level set of the plotted field is triangulated with marching cubes and drawn as a shaded, depth-tested mesh instead of a `Makie.volume`. The volume `algorithm=:iso` ray-marches the shell `isovalue ± isorange`, so its surfaces look striped, and the other volume algorithms are drawn without depth (`viz!` sets `enable_depth=false`), so the body is always drawn over the flow. The mesh has neither problem, and with a translucent colour and `transparency=true` the body stays visible through it. ```julia using WaterLily, GLMakie, Meshing viz!(sim; f=ω!, isomesh=12, color=RGBAf(0.35, 0.55, 0.8, 0.5), transparency=true, body2mesh=true) ``` *Developed sphere flow (WaterLily-Benchmarks `sphere_5_Float32.jld2`: D=32, 512×192×192 cells, Re=3700, tU/D=50), vorticity magnitude |ω|D/U with `body2mesh=true`. Level 12 includes the boundary layer, so the plots also show how each mode handles a field that wraps the body. Top: side view, bottom: downstream view. `:mip` and `:iso` use the `viz!` defaults (`enable_depth=false` for `:mip`, depth on for `:iso`).* ## Changes - `isosurface_mesh(a, level)` in `WaterLilyMeshingExt` (declared in core next to `get_body`): marching cubes to a `GeometryBasics.Mesh`, empty if the field does not cross `level`. `get_body(sdf, Val(true))` now calls it with level 0, so the body and the field share the triangulation. - `viz!(...; isomesh=nothing)`: when set, the field Observable is lifted to `isosurface_mesh(σ, isomesh)` and plotted by a new `plot_σ_obs!` method for meshes, and `kwargs` go to `Makie.mesh!` (eg. `color`, `transparency`, `backlight`). The forced `enable_depth=false` is skipped, `d=3` is asserted, and Meshing must be loaded, as for `body2mesh`. - The field mesh uses `backlight=1` by default. Marching cubes orients the normals towards increasing values, so they point into the region of interest for vorticity or -λ₂ and out of it for low pressure. Lighting both sides removes the dependence on the sign: with `backlight=0` a vorticity surface is lit from behind and renders dark (see the gallery). - Docstring: `isomesh`, plus the existing `enable_depth=false` default for non-iso volumes and how to depth-test (`enable_depth=true`) and blend (`transparency=true` with a translucent colormap) the volume with the body. - `assets/waterlily_watermark.png` (706×299) and `assets/waterlily_watermark_2x.png` (1228×520): a WaterLily card to overlay on videos, eg. `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -i waterlily_watermark.png -filter_complex "overlay=W-w-40:H-h-40" out.mp4`. ![WaterLily watermark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WaterLily-jl/WaterLily.jl/dc6e5f2a85a438eea55da687fc68723a0b42eaab/assets/waterlily_watermark_2x.png) ## Cost Per-frame cost without the simulation step, as medians over 5 snapshots 0.5 D/U apart (after a warm-up), on the full 512×192×192 domain with `body2mesh=true` and about 2400×2166 px frames (RTX 4060 8 GB, 8 threads). `update` is `viz_step!` without a time step (field function, body update and field-to-plot conversion), and `render` is the draw plus readback. | method | update (s) | render (s) | total (s) | |---|---|---|---| | `:mip` | 0.92 | 0.10 | 1.02 | | `:mip`, `enable_depth` + `transparency` | 0.92 | 0.09 | 1.01 | | `:iso` | 0.90 | 0.10 | 1.00 | | `:absorption` | 0.87 | 0.05 | 0.92 | | `isomesh` | 1.48 | 0.016 | 1.50 | | `isomesh`, α=0.5 + `transparency` | 1.47 | 0.025 | 1.49 | Common to all methods: the field function (|ω| on the GPU plus the copy to the CPU) takes 0.03 s and the body mesh 0.68 s. `isomesh` adds the marching cubes of the field, 0.65 s for about 52k triangles, so about 0.5 s more per frame than the volumes (2.5 time steps of this case at 0.2 s each), while its draw is the cheapest. Both marching cubes run single-threaded on the CPU over the plotted region, so cropping with `CIs` reduces them, and `remeasure=false` skips the body mesh for static bodies. ## Gallery Every combination of the options in `viz!` for 3D fields, on the same snapshot. Only `:mip`, `:iso` and `:absorption` apply to `viz!`: its field function fills a float array, while `:absorptionrgba` and `:additive` expect RGBA volumes and `:indexedabsorption` expects integers (`:additive` renders the red channel in an opaque box).

:mip with enable_depth=true and transparency=true, opaque vs translucent colormap *Top: -λ₂(D/U)² zeroed within 4 cells of the body, bottom: |ω|D/U.*
What the gallery shows: - `enable_depth=false`, the default for `:mip` and `:absorption`: the body is always drawn over the field, also where the boundary layer wraps it. - `enable_depth=true`: `:mip` and `:absorption` hide the body under the boundary layer. It shows through only with a translucent colormap and `transparency=true`, and `lowclip=:transparent` then punches holes in the body where the field is below the colour range. - `:iso`: correct depth, but the surfaces are striped. - `isomesh`: correct depth and smooth surfaces in all cases. The boundary-layer shell opens at the front stagnation region, where the body shows through. - `body2mesh=false`: the body itself is a ray-marched iso volume and shows the same rings. - Passing `enable_depth` with `isomesh` errors in Makie ("Invalid attribute enable_depth for plot type Mesh"): mesh plots are always depth-tested. ## Tests Checked by hand on a small sphere and on the developed benchmark sphere: opaque and translucent `isomesh` with a meshed and a volume body over several frames, a level with no surface (empty mesh), a low-pressure surface (region of interest below the level), the default MIP and `body2mesh` alone after the `get_body` refactor, the `d=2` assertion, and a user `plot_σ_obs!` override (as in the propeller example) not being reached. There are no automated tests: Makie is not in the test targets, as for the rest of `viz!`. ## Not in this PR - `viz!` keeps every figure in `_fig_steppers` for `viz_step!`, so repeated calls in one session keep all figures and their buffers alive. Rendering this gallery in one session ran out of RAM until the entries were deleted and `GLMakie.closeall()` was called after each render. - The marching cubes could be restricted to the bounding box of the cells above the level, or threaded. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
